title: every Page has a face, even without a photo

criteria.text: The photo step is optional; composer completes without one
criteria.note: `PagePhotoPicker` rides in the About step of `SellWalkthrough`; `update_draft` takes `photoUrl` (null clears, undefined leaves alone); a failed upload does not trap the member [V build log t145, files]. #598 Checked: unmarked: `PagePhotoPicker.test.tsx` ("never blocks the step").

criteria.text: Stored bytes carry no metadata, GPS included, verified against the file
criteria.note: Canvas resize plus WebP re-encode strips it; bucket accepts `image/webp` only (`039_media_bucket.sql`). Missing: a check on an object read back from the bucket. #598 Checked: unmarked: `upload-image.test.ts:112` (real GPS fixture, byte-level, but on pipeline output, not a stored object).

criteria.text: A raw upload that bypasses the client is rejected by the storage API
criteria.note: Bucket `allowed_mime_types` webp, 5MB limit, insert/update/delete scoped to own `{member_id}/` prefix [V migration]. #598 Checked: unmarked: `tests/media-bucket-storage-api.test.ts` (JPEG, SVG, over 5MB, other member's prefix); runs only when `requireRunnable` passes, CI run unknown.

criteria.text: No photo shows the kind's default art, identical for every viewer; missing Page picture falls back to it
criteria.note: Built half: `DefaultArt` by kind (shop, service, group) on the Page, browse cards and post cards, with the Page-picture fallback in `PagePosts` [V]. Missing: the signed-out withheld card draws a plain tile with no icon, so not identical to every viewer. #335 (open, Beta 11-06) Checked: unmarked: `DefaultArt.test.tsx`.

criteria.text: Operator removes a Page's photo in one action; object deleted, event recorded
criteria.note: Built half: report-driven reversible removal (`photo_removed_at`) in the admin queue, then a separate `report.purge_target` plus `report.purge` that deletes the object and writes a `photo_purges` row with who, why and when (#491, migration `20261007250000`) [V]. Missing: one action (removal keeps the bytes; deletion is a second, deliberate act per `docs/purge-proposal.md`), and the record is a `photo_purges` row, not an event [A].
